chapter: The Blakey quartet on the road
title: Forming the quartet with Art Blakey at Birdland
summary: The Birdland house band of Blakey, Kenny Drew and Eugene Wright became his touring quartet.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Playing in Lionel Hampton's big band

blocks.x: So in ’52, I guess that would be after you disbanded the big band.
That’s when you first came into contact with Art Blakey. Is that right?
And that became a really important collaboration.

I had a job at the Birdland, you know, as a soloist. And the house band was Art Blakey, Kenny Drew, and Eugene Wright. And from the first note we gelled, it was picnic, everybody liked it and we, and by the end of that engagement, I think it was two weeks I had Birdland, I said to Art, “Lets make a group out of this and go out.” And Art said, “Yeah, lets do it.” So we did, we became a bona fide traveling group. And did well most of the time.
Known as the “Buddy DeFranco Quartet.” Right…
Buddy DeFranco… Murphy:…and a lot of people mistake that as you playing with Blakey’s group, is that right?

Yeah, there’s even a recording that I did with Art that I did on bass clarinet and Art Blakey was in the group. And later on they turned out the same CD with Art Blakey featuring Buddy DeFranco. And a lot of people used to say to me many years later, “Oh, I remember when you played with Art Blakey’s group.” And when that wasn’t
it, it was my group and featuring Art Blakey. Good experience, Art was, he was something.
Why musically did you gel so well do you think?

Oh, I think that because of the intensity of the music and the feeling. That group was hot, it really was. It was every bit as hot as the group on Jazz at the Philharmonic and that was with Oscar Peterson, Ray Brown, and Louie Bellson or Buddy Rich. It was hot. That group with Art Blakey was really intense, you couldn’t miss the message.
